newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods mixed but exports lend support.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods mixed but exports lend support.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices ended narrowly mixed following a quiet Friday session, as exports from the region lent support despite falling values for futures, traders said.
A cargo of conventional gasoline was shipped from San Francisco to the U.S. Gulf Thursday, while a ship a high-octane blending component was slated to leave today, traders said.
West Coast gasoline prices have fallen relative to the rest of the U.S in the last six weeks, prompting shippers to send the region's excess supply elsewhere for profit.
"I would guess we won't go much lower," said one California-based broker.
As refiners suffer low margins, they have also begun to cut runs, with Tosco scaling back crude use for the last two weeks and Chevron reportedly trimming runs this week, traders said.

Gasoline stocks meanwhile fell by a neutral 166,000 barrels to 29.4 million barrels and distillate stocks fell by 224,000 barrels to 11.7 million barrels, according to trade group American Petroleum Institute.

ARCO said it brought back its 43,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker, a distillate-mkaing unit, which has been shut since May 2. The returning unit caused flaring and has forced the refinery to trim some output.
Regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline was pegged between 62.50 and 63.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, down 0.25 cents from Thursday. San Francisco dropped 0.50 cents to 62.50/63.50 cents.
Regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was pegged at between 60 and 61 cents a gallon, up one cent from Thursday.
Refineries continued to operate normally, , with most refineries operating normally.
++ DISTILLATE prices in Los Angeles were steady to lower, with CARB-grade low sulphur, low aromatic diesel pegged 0.50 cents a gallon weaker at 64/65 cents a gallon.
EPA-grade diesel was steady at 58/59 cents.
Two cargoes of EPA were scheduled to leave the San Francisco area for Asia next week.
